targetText: The extension of Freudian hypotheses seems 'educated', even scientific, but it is ignorant, bungling. Freudian theory is the modern fashion.
summary: Lenin critiques bourgeois psychoanalytic fashions that replace materialist class analysis with individualist sexual speculation.
explanation: Lenin argues that fashionable Freudian pamphlets flourishing in bourgeois society divert working-class activists away from collective struggle into self-absorbed individual psychology.

targetText: Forms of marriage and of the family, in their historical development and dependence upon economic life, are calculated to destroy the superstition existing in the minds of working women concerning the eternal character of bourgeois society.
summary: Zetkin demonstrates that studying the historical evolution of the family exposes capitalism as a temporary, changeable system.
explanation: Drawing on Engels's Origin of the Family, Zetkin points out that when working women learn how family structures change across economic modes of production, they realize bourgeois property relations are not eternal.

targetText: The great social question appears as an adjunct, a part, of sexual problems. The main thing becomes a subsidiary matter. That not only endangers clarity on that question itself, it muddles the thoughts, the class-consciousness of proletarian women generally.
summary: Treating class struggle as secondary to personal sexual theories confuses working-class consciousness.
explanation: Lenin warns that isolating sex and marriage from the struggle against capitalist exploitation inverts Marxist priorities and weakens revolutionary focus during acute political crises.
